issues_confirmed: standalone/places_scraper.py:185-187,209 — a PlacesApiError from get_place_details is swallowed per-place by `except Exception: continue`, the inner loop ends with saved==0, and mark_done() at :209 still runs. area_manager.py:13-22 then treats the area as done for rescrape_days (30), so a denied key or OVER_QUERY_LIMIT mid-area permanently poisons Resume for that city×term. PR #1 (fac30b0) closed this on the Text Search path only, because run_places_scrape:160-162 does `continue` before mark_done.
standalone/places_scraper.py:168-169 — cancelling mid-area calls mark_done(saved), writing off every place not yet processed in that area for 30 days.
standalone/places_scraper.py:183-184 — BillingLimitError mid-area does the same.

standalone/models.py:48-53 — ScrapedArea has only id/scraped_at/result_count, no completeness field, so result_count=0 from a failed area is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty city. standalone/db.py:32-34 uses create_all, which never adds columns, so adding one would raise `no such column` on existing client DBs.

.github/workflows/build-exe.yml — the Package step Copy-Items only config.ini/README.md/SETUP_GUIDE.pdf and Compress-Archive lists exactly four files; cities_us.txt is absent. supplier_scraper.spec:15-16 bundles it into _MEIPASS, but web_server.py:32 is the only _MEIPASS read site and covers templates/ only, so the bundled copy is unreachable from cli.py:28, web_server.py:567 and :631, which all read Path(sys.executable).parent / 'cities_us.txt'.

standalone/web_server.py:150-157 — _sent_today() compares EmailLog.created_at against local midnight (datetime.combine(date.today(), min.time())), but rows are written naive-UTC at web_server.py:538 and cli.py:371. At UTC+5 the daily cap counts 0 between local 00:00 and 05:00, so the pre-flight check at :486 and the in-loop re-check at :513 both pass unconditionally.

standalone/cli.py:311-383 — the send command applies no daily cap at all: no _daily_cap(), no _sent_today(), only throttle pacing at cli.py:325 (default 30/min vs web_server.py:491's 20/min). README.md:34 instructs the client to use this path.

standalone/cli.py:258-267 — `scrape --resume` without --city or --all-us falls through to the else branch and sys.exit(1) with 'Specify --city or --all-us', despite cli.py:9 and the --resume help at :231 documenting it as a standalone command.

README.md:74,81,83 — still name the update manifest `version.json`; the live constant at standalone/update_checker.py:15 is `Supplier_Scraper.json` (fixed in a08e1a3). update_checker.py:47-48 swallows every exception, so a wrong filename 404s silently.

standalone/billing_guard.py:4-9,24-25 — docstring and constants assert a flat 10,000 calls/month/endpoint free tier matching neither the legacy shared $200 credit nor the post-2025 per-SKU tiers; :60-63 nonetheless tells the client it is 'Stopping to avoid charges.' README.md:47 repeats the number.
standalone/billing_guard.py:64 — the counter is incremented inside _check_and_increment, i.e. before the HTTP request at places_scraper.py:44 and :71, so a timeout consumes budget.

standalone/places_scraper.py:28 — DETAILS_FIELDS includes `rating`, the only top-tier-priced field, which drags every Place Details call into that tier. google_rating is written at :111 and declared at models.py:33 but read nowhere: no template, no scorer, no CSV export.

standalone/requirements_standalone.txt:6-7 — pins beautifulsoup4==4.12.3 and lxml>=5.2.1; neither is imported anywhere in standalone/ (extraction is regex, website_email_extractor.py:8). lxml is unpinned in the pipeline that builds the client artifact.

No CI runs the tests — build-exe.yml triggers only on v*.*.* tags and only builds the exe. The test_places_scraper.py added by PR #1 has never been executed (its own PR body states the sandbox lacked sqlalchemy/httpx); same today, no venv is present and `import sqlalchemy` fails.
standalone/cities_us.txt — 13 duplicate entries out of 267 non-comment lines, each costing a redundant Text Search per term.

standalone/web_server.py:578-581 vs :641 and cli.py:94-96 — _scrape_page_ctx counts every non-comment line as a city while both consumers require a comma, so the progress denominator and the real city list can diverge (all 267 current lines have a comma, so it does not bite today).

verdict: Solid, genuinely working product with one severe correctness hole and one release-packaging hole that have each outlived multiple reviews; the code is well-organised and readable, but six weeks idle and zero CI mean nothing here is verified — including the test that shipped with the last fix.
